Pushed: your Desk lines now wait up to a minute for a busy agent instead of bouncing, and say 'Sending…' meanwhile. The node retries with backoff and caps any app's wait at 10 minutes. Hard-refresh Desk to get it. Also in: the names appServerPost() and appServerReply() are written into G17.

Built on Andy's go: peer.post takes an optional patienceMs, capped at 10 min, passed to router.post as how. The shell forwards opts.patienceMs, and Desk and DeskDetails use 60 s. hubPost.js checks the pass-through and the cap. Your tests from earlier: busy then delivered within patience, unreachable fails at once. Commit: 222ec545.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's join vs appFaceApp question.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- your join vs appFaceApp question.

Yes, that's the difference, and it's a clean one. appFaceApp is the GRANTING side; join is one of those it grants to. appFaceApp holds the mapping, subdomain to whoever asked, in grants.json on your own node ('A name grant persists. true. but only on the owners node'). join is an app-server process on your box that asks for the name 'join', exactly as Alice would ask for 'alice' ('there is no system-face special case'). The row it gets is { join: { to: <join's key> } }. That row IS the route. When a browser asks join.spirit.andyflinn.com: the VPS appFaceApp knows nothing about apps. It just forwards the request with its host to your node (appServerPost). On your node the forwarder reads the host's row, finds join's key, and hands the request to that process. So the VPS never holds the table, and your node never guesses. What's owed there, in the forwarder: turning a granted key into the local process that holds it (its port today, its named pipe after G18).

Fixed and verified: your lines no longer get lost to a busy agent. Desk now asks for a minute of patience on every send, so a 'busy' is retried instead of ending it (claude-windows, 222ec54; checked, and the checks fail if the fix is taken out).
